video_title: Marcus Banks Exposes The Dark Side Of The NBA

quotes.speaker: Marcus Banks
quotes.summary_phrase: Marcus Banks on his struggle to build relationships in the NBA
quotes.excerpt: I didn't do the right things necessary when it comes to creating relationships, right? Because I was in competition
quotes.quote: The way I took care of my body, the way I understood and respected the game, my career should have been so much longer. But I didn't do the right things necessary when it comes to creating relationships, right? Because I was in competition with these motherfuckers. Excuse me. You understand? I wanted to be like Mike Bibby. You understand? I wanted to wear all the Jordans. I wanted to be like BD. Guess what? Come down. I dreamed of these different things every night while I was playing this game.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Banks
quotes.summary_phrase: Marcus Banks on why big recruits struggle in Las Vegas
quotes.excerpt: Guys from out of town don't do well here. Like if they're big recruits, they come here, they do not do well here because of the lights.
quotes.quote: To be honest, guys from out of town don't do well here. Like if they're big recruits, they come here, they do not do well here because of the lights. Because you come from the country and you've never seen the stuff that's out here, this place don't sleep. So you have to be extremely disciplined and you have to actually know the kids who you're going to get. So a lot of kids that came here, man, ended up living here, never going back home and different things like that because those lights never shut off. It's access 24 hours to whatever you'd like to do. So a lot of people call this home now.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Banks
quotes.summary_phrase: Marcus Banks on the lack of NBA presence in Las Vegas
quotes.excerpt: I've never seen an NBA player until I think it was Nick Van Exel, Sam Cassell, I can't remember the point guard name from St. John's.
quotes.quote: We didn't get that out here. This is not a sports town and it wasn't. So we didn't have, like I've never seen an NBA player until I think it was Nick Van Exel, Sam Cassell, I can't remember the point guard name from St. John's. What was his name? Not Mark Jackson, not Mark Jackson, not Saterfield. Who was the other guard? Eric Barkley. Eric Barkley. Okay, so remember he went to Portland. Okay, so those guys used to come here in Vegas and this is when I was at UNLV. So you got to think I've never seen an NBA player.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Banks
quotes.summary_phrase: Marcus Banks on his recruitment to Dixie State and Michigan
quotes.excerpt: I know you guys know Kevin Gaines and Demetrius Hunter. D Hunt went to Georgetown, Kevin Gaines went off to Michigan and I went off to Dixie.
quotes.quote: I used to, these two kids that go here, I know you guys know Kevin Gaines and Demetrius Hunter. D Hunt went to Georgetown, Kevin Gaines went off to Michigan and I went off to Dixie. Right, so that was my first fuel. So I took a guy here by the name of Eddie Shelby, I took him down and we end up winning Nationals there. But I cried every single day, right, to get out of the dungeon. And that's what I call it. Like it's like being overseas, right, and to get back to Division I, you got to grind out. And remember guys, look, JC was where all the best athletes was. Yeah, yeah. Like you guys want to talk about a dog, go to junior college. All 12 to 15 of those guys are dogs because all their motives is the same, to try to get to Division I.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Banks
quotes.summary_phrase: Marcus Banks on his academic ineligibility in high school
quotes.excerpt: I've never done a homework assignment with my parents. You know, so I didn't understand how to apply myself.
quotes.quote: I was ineligible from eighth grade all the way up to high school. And people be like, Mark, why, what happened? I've never done a homework assignment with my parents. You know, so I didn't understand how to apply myself. Right, so I think my junior year, I went to summer school and I took PE, weight training. So I got three A's and you know, three A's equate to like, so that's like, you know, that remove any grade that you had. So during the school year, I had a couple grades that I can, like art and whatever. So by the time the season started, all you got to do is be eligible when it's starting. And it's like two weeks you have to do some work. Oh man, that was a chico for me.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Banks
quotes.summary_phrase: Marcus Banks on being drafted by the Celtics
quotes.excerpt: I worked out for two teams. I knew I was going to be drafted to the Celtics within two weeks out of school.
quotes.quote: I worked out for two teams. I knew I was going to be drafted to the Celtics within two weeks out of school. Because I went to the first workout, I don't think I missed a shot. Danny Ainge called me in the office and was like, you've been, you know, working on your game. So this is the part where I get to Spoonhour and that coach Derek Thomas and you know, little J Spoon, they had me prepared. I didn't even know what I was preparing for. Damn. And you know, of course you go over with the guys where they think you're going to get drafted, right? And you of course you book all your trips all summer long. I went to LA for like two weeks. I worked out with all the top, probably 15 players.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Banks
quotes.summary_phrase: Marcus Banks on the 2003 draft class
quotes.excerpt: I think it was, first guard was Heinrich, of course D-Wade, TJ Ford, Ridnour, myself, I think Mo Williams was in that draft.
quotes.quote: I think it was, first guard was Heinrich, of course D-Wade, TJ Ford, Ridnour, myself, I think Mo Williams was in that draft. Um, so that draft was a draft full of guards. Right, so they sent us all, Troy Bell, all of those guys, they sent us all to LA. They rolled the ball out there. Man, when I tell you I ate everybody alive to the point where, you know, TJ and those guys got drafted 5, 7, 8. When the scouts and everybody came in the gym, Marcus sit down. So I was like, what? What am I doing here? Like and I honestly got a story, right? So they sent me home. My agent Mike Higgins was like, look, um, they want you to come home. Yeah. He was like, they want you to come home. So I was like, come home, man, I'm preparing for the draft, like what's going on? And he was like, just come back home. You got to work out in Boston.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Banks
quotes.summary_phrase: Marcus Banks on his pre-draft workout in Boston
quotes.excerpt: I went down to Boston and they had four guys in there. I can't even remember, I think it was maybe Will Bynum, Omar Cook, Lenny Cooke.
quotes.quote: I went down to Boston and they had four guys in there. I can't even remember, I think it was maybe Will Bynum, Omar Cook, Lenny Cooke. He was there, they had a Troy Bell, a couple of those guys from DC all in the area. And you know, you did a lot of one-on-one. So for me, to show everybody how horror I was, I don't want no offense. All defense. Let's go, one-on-one, full court. They couldn't even get the ball past half. And at that time, you know, I had a little 40 inch, 42, so I'm ripping these guys. Monkey dunking. Boom. I'm talking about, like you know how we used to like make a statement where you not, you know, right now they just and get out of there. No, we was boom and shaking the rim, right? And sit right back down on them. Right, so they was like, where is this kid being? Who represent him? Like you know what I'm saying? So now it's starting to kind of wake up. So they call me upstairs. So I sat down with OB, that's Jim O'Brien. Jim O'Brien, yeah, yeah. He was the head coach at the time. Danny Ainge and they was like, look, um, we want to draft you at 13 but you're not going to be there. We need to figure out a way to move. It was that transparent. Wow. So I came into the business, right? In the business involved in the business, didn't even understand it.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Banks
quotes.summary_phrase: Marcus Banks on his draft night experience
quotes.excerpt: Draft night, draft night, um, you know it's in New York or whatever. Um, they like you can't go.
quotes.quote: Draft night, draft night, um, you know it's in New York or whatever. Um, they like you can't go. My agent was like, you are not allowed at the draft. I'm like, what the hell is going on? Right, so they like, look, just had a biggest party that you can have at home, invite all your friends and whatever, whatever, you good. So I'm like, all right, cool. So I'm watching the draft go on. So then years later, they was like, do you really understand why you couldn't go to the draft? And I was like, no. He was like, at that time you would have affected the draft board. So they see you in the lottery, the green room. What is this guy doing here? And he's supposed to go second round. So that really, I didn't get a chance to shake hands and come across and rep Vegas and you know what I'm saying? So it was more like, stay at home. If you go, you're going to disrupt the draft. So they was like, because it was so many point guards. Right. Meaning teams would have seen you in the green room and would start doing research and for that, we should draft. Okay.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Banks
quotes.summary_phrase: Marcus Banks on his relationship with Floyd Mayweather
quotes.excerpt: Me and Floyd started together. Like we met each other, I was 18, I think he was 24.
quotes.quote: Me and Floyd started together. Like we met each other, I was 18, I think he was 24. So if you go back to a lot of his fights, I'm in the ring, you know what I'm saying? Like all these belts. Like no, we was like, I'm talking about best friends in the whole world. Okay. I put Floyd on basketball. This is the reason why he used to come to UNLV and watch me every day. Yeah. So our relationship we started, so he'll go box and we'll leave there and go hoop. Okay. So that's, that's what it was. So his whole, we just partied, like we rented out a spot. He came through, man, it was amazing. It was just so many people. I can't even right now, you understand, it's pressure, but everybody showed up. You know what I'm saying? So they made up of me not going to the draft and everything like that. So it was really cool.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Banks
quotes.summary_phrase: Marcus Banks on his NBA welcome moment
quotes.excerpt: I don't, I'm not the guy to have idols and shit like that. Like my dad's my idol.
quotes.quote: For me, um, I think it was just being there. Like I don't, I'm not the guy to have idols and shit like that. Like my dad's my idol. You know what I'm saying? He a hard working man, you know what I'm saying? We came from nothing. Right. So I didn't, I didn't idolize, you know, people. You know what I'm saying? I I had it right there in front of me. Mhm. So that's what, you know, helps me be the person I am today. You know what I'm saying? If that makes sense, right? That's perfect sense. Um, so when I came into the NBA, I took it, you know, as my job. I took it as a course, like these guys on TV. So that first go around, you be like, damn like that's Iverson right there. You know, and I know he says a lot, you know what I'm saying, about, you know, he went to sleep early when I defend him or play against him or whatever, but playing against these guys like, Mike, um, Stefan Marbury, Allen Iverson, Baron Davis, Steve Nash, Jason Kidd, man, our era was crazy. So those was those nights that I never slept. You understand? These guys get a break because not every defender is going to pick you up full court. But for me, my job was to test every single one of those guys. Yeah. If that makes sense. Yeah.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Banks
quotes.summary_phrase: Using two pound weights to build defensive hand endurance
quotes.excerpt: So you have to struggle. So imagine if I dropped them weights and put my hands up
quotes.quote: So what he used to do, I used to take two pound weights and just hold them. Keep your hands up. I'm talking about crying, bubbling, right? So you put them down, we're going to go another minute. So you have to struggle. So imagine if I dropped them weights and put my hands up, you see how easy that is? So it was just a mind thing because these things are really only two pounds. So he tricked me with a lot of little different things.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Banks
quotes.summary_phrase: Hard work and backyard chores building a defensive mindset
quotes.excerpt: I never cheated this. You understand? So the entire backyard before I go play basketball
quotes.quote: People wonder why I wanted to play defense. Well, he only had me outside cutting the acre backyard with the push mower. This is before you had the button. You see how hard it is outside. This is my life for real. I never cheated this. You understand? So the entire backyard before I go play basketball, before I go with my friends.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Banks
quotes.summary_phrase: Marcus Banks recalls Paul Pierce's intense early morning workout habits
quotes.excerpt: I pull up to the practice facility and all you hear is the treadmill going.
quotes.quote: I pull up to the practice facility and all you hear is the treadmill going. So I'm like, I thought I was the first person here. It's one of your main guys there. He's up there working out. We got practice at 11, it's like eight. So he getting it in. So all I wanted to do, I told you I was a workhorse, I just needed somebody to follow. I go up there, it was just the person I was looking for. So I'm like, what's happening in square? You know who square is? Paul Pierce, PP. That's who we call him square. Because he a square. I'm like, what's up square? And all you can hear, you know how treadmill sounds when you're getting your work in. He was tripping. So I'm like, what you doing? Get out of here, rookie. What are you doing here? And I was like, wait, what? So instantly, I'm, what you mean? And he was like, just come back home, you got to work out in Boston.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Banks
quotes.summary_phrase: Marcus Banks reflects on Paul Pierce's status as a hometown hero
quotes.excerpt: He was like a superhero to us. And he's from Sunny South Dallas.
quotes.quote: I went down to Boston and they had four guys in there. I think it was maybe Will Bynum, Omar Cook, Lenny Cooke, Stefan Smith, all them playing on the middle court. And it was us kids just watching them around and he was like a superhero to us. And he's from Sunny South Dallas. He don't play no games. And he was just everything so when he won it, the entire hood celebrated, man. It was super dope.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Banks
quotes.summary_phrase: Marcus Banks describes the intense atmosphere playing for Panathinaikos in Greece
quotes.excerpt: They treat you like Jordan. They never seen one of us before anyway.
quotes.quote: I went over in France. Michael Batiste was over there but he was retired. He came back. He was playing for another team they offered him money. So I was over there with Sofoklis, the Shaquille O'Neal from over there. Yeah, big fella. He was there and then Theo Papaloukas. So like the best, some of the best guards you going to like, defense guy. Man, these guys, listen, don't believe that. I lived with these guys over there, man, it wasn't like you think. Like, no defense and I mean, they control their stats. But I seen a lot. I played against Mike when he was at Panathinaikos. They love Mike over there. So, you got to think, OAKA fit 32,000 people. Man, look, if y'all want to understand the best experience in my life, it was going to play overseas. Don't get it twisted. I got a story where they treat you like Jordan. They never seen one of us before anyway. So I went over there, man, and I'm not married or nothing like that. Fresh, like, man, this guy coming from the NBA. So, it was crazy. They had police barricades to every single game. Like, boy, it was the best experience.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Banks
quotes.summary_phrase: The intense rivalry between Panathinaikos and Olympiacos in Greece
quotes.excerpt: So really, in the states, guys, that's like Bloods versus Crips. No doubt.
quotes.quote: We played against Olympiacos and it was Panathinaikos. So really, in the states, guys, that's like Bloods versus Crips. No doubt. So we had to have the game unit in this. I'm talking about, we went through the city like presidents. But guess what, we get to the gym, man, they shooting fireworks, they got fish bombs in there. So imagine being at the free throw line and a bomb go off in the gym. I'm talking about live smoke, I'm talking about everything, they throwing them on the court. We played in a cage. We played in the net cage, let me tell you. The greatest atmosphere in the world. Like you know how over here, a guy fly through the air, skip through, do a craziest move, dunk the ball. Check them. Let it happen over there. They running on the court. I'm talking about they have Roman candles. You know the fireworks? That's what shooting in the stands. I'm talking about smoking cigarettes the whole time. It's a cloud over the court. It's completely different. The game starts at 10:00 at night too by the way.
